page: Vultr vhf-12c-48gb is an x86_64 architecture server within the High Frequency Compute family. It features 12 shared vCPUs mapped to 6 physical Intel CPU cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 48.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled with a 768 GB NVMe SSD, and the configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance type.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU metrics in the top 25% and single-threaded gzip compression achieving top-tier status in the top 10%. Multi-core CPU performance and PassMark CPU scores sit in the middle 50% average range. Memory performance shows a stark contrast: while the PassMark memory score ranks in the top 10% and cached small-block read bandwidth is average, large-block uncached read and write memory bandwidths fall into the bottom 25%.

Given its shared CPU allocation, this server offers a cost-efficient profile for workloads that require high single-threaded performance but do not demand continuous, dedicated multi-core execution. It is well-suited for tasks such as single-threaded file compression, general-purpose web serving, and moderate database operations. However, the weak uncached memory bandwidth and shared CPU resources make it less optimal for memory-intensive data processing or sustained multi-threaded workloads.
